#include <bits/stdc++.h>
using namespace std;

static int mod = 998244353;
const int MAX_K = 20;

vector<long long> clean(const vector<long long>& a) {
    int i;
    for (i = (int)a.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
        if (a[i] != 0) {
            if (i == (int)a.size() - 1) return a;
            return vector<long long>(a.begin(), a.begin() + i + 1);
        }
    }
    return vector<long long>();
}

vector<long long> mulnaive(const vector<long long>& a, const vector<long long>& b) {
    vector<long long> c(a.size() + b.size() - 1, 0);
    long long big = 8LL * mod * mod;
    for (size_t i = 0; i < a.size(); ++i) {
        for (size_t j = 0; j < b.size(); ++j) {
            c[i + j] += a[i] * b[j];
            if (c[i + j] >= big) c[i + j] -= big;
        }
    }
    for (auto& val : c) {
        val %= mod;
    }
    return c;
}

// Polynomial convolution via NTT
// For simplicity, we implement the convolution simply via naive multiplication 

long long pow_mod(long long a, long long n, long long p) {
    long long ret = 1;
    for (; n > 0; n >>= 1) {
        if (n & 1) ret = ret * a % p;
        a = a * a % p;
    }
    return ret;
}

long long invl(long long a, long long p) {
    // Fermat's little theorem, since p is prime
    return pow_mod(a, p - 2, p);
}

// Implement a naive polynomial convolution for small sizes
vector<long long> convoluteSimply(const vector<long long>& a, const vector<long long>& b, int P, int g) {
    int m = 1;
    int n = max((int)a.size(), (int)b.size());
    while (m < n) m <<= 1;
    vector<long long> fa(a), fb(b);
    fa.resize(m); fb.resize(m);
    // optional: apply NTT here; for the new implementation, can fallback to naive if small
    vector<long long> res(m * 2 -1, 0);
    for (int i = 0; i < (int)a.size(); ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < (int)b.size(); ++j) {
            res[i + j] += a[i] * b[j];
        }
    }
    for (auto& val : res) val %= P;
    return res;
}

int main() {
    ios::sync_with_stdio(false);
    cin.tie(nullptr);

    int n; cin >> n;
    int K; cin >> K;
    vector<int> d(K);
    for (int& di : d) cin >> di;

    vector<long long> f(20, 0);
    for (int i = 0; i < K; ++i) {
        for (int j = 0; j < K; ++j) {
            int index = 10 + d[i] - d[j];
            f[index] += 1;
        }
    }

    n /= 2;
    vector<long long> g(1,1);

    for (int D =17; D >=0; --D) {
        // Depending on the size, convolution could be optimized, but here simplified
        g = clean(convoluteSimply(g, g, mod, 3));
        if ((n << (~D)) < 0) {

        }
    }

    if ((size_t)(n*10) < g.size()) cout << g[n*10] << "\n" ;
    else cout << 0 << "\n";

    return 0;
}
